lede: There are millions of carbon compounds, and you are not asked to learn them one by one. They come in families whose members differ by one CH₂ at a time, so learning how one member behaves tells you about all of them.
can: Give the four features of a homologous series, and define a hydrocarbon.
Use CnH2n+2 to write the formula of any alkane.
Draw the displayed formula of methane, ethane, propane and butane.

text: Homologous series, hydrocarbons and the alkanes

md: There are millions of carbon compounds, which sounds impossible to learn. It is not, because they come in families. Learn how one family behaves and you know every member of it, including ones you have never seen.

prompt: In the table above, which alkane has the longest carbon chain?
explain: Butane, with four carbons. The names run methane, ethane, propane, butane as the chain grows.

md: Every carbon atom forms **four covalent bonds** — no more, no fewer. That one rule builds every structure in this topic, and it is how you check your own drawing: count the lines at each carbon and there must be four. A **displayed formula** shows **every** bond as a line, so methane is a C with four lines to four H atoms.

prompt: In the displayed formula of methane above, how many bonds are drawn from the carbon atom?
explain: Four. Carbon always forms four bonds, and checking that count is the quickest way to catch a wrong structure.

title: Why the properties change gradually
md: Each step along the family adds one more CH₂ to the chain. Bigger molecules attract each other more strongly, so it takes more energy to pull them apart and the boiling point rises. The chemistry stays the same because the bonds in the molecule are the same kind; only the size has changed.

prompt: Members of a homologous series differ from the next one along by a ______ group.
explain: CH₂. One more carbon and two more hydrogens each time, which is why the general formula works.

md:
A **hydrocarbon** is a compound that consists of hydrogen and carbon **only**. That word *only* is worth a mark on its own, and it is the one examiners report being dropped year after year.
The **alkanes** are the hydrocarbon family with the general formula $\ce{C_nH_{2n+2}}$. They are **saturated**: every bond is a single bond. The first four are **methane**, **ethane**, **propane** and **butane**, and all four are **gases** at room temperature.

prompt: Which of these is the full definition of a hydrocarbon?
options: a compound that consists of hydrogen and carbon only
a compound that contains hydrogen and carbon
a molecule made of hydrogen, carbon and oxygen
answer: a compound that consists of hydrogen and carbon only
explain: The word only is the second mark. Ethanol contains hydrogen and carbon too, and it is not a hydrocarbon, because it has oxygen as well.

text: 4. Worked example: from a name to a structure

md:
**The question.** Draw the displayed formula of propane and give its molecular formula. **[3]**
**Step 1 — read the chain length from the name.** *Prop* means three carbons: meth 1, eth 2, prop 3, but 4.
**Step 2 — draw the carbon chain first.** Three C atoms in a row, joined by single bonds, because an alkane is saturated.

prompt: Finish step 2. In the displayed formula of propane above, how many carbon-to-carbon bonds join the three carbons?
explain: Two: one between the first and second carbon, one between the second and third. Three carbons in a chain always need two bonds to link them.

md:
**Step 3 — fill every spare bond with a hydrogen.** The end carbons have used one bond each, so they take **three** H. The middle carbon has used two, so it takes **two**. That gives 3 + 2 + 3 = 8 hydrogens.
**Step 4 — write the molecular formula.** Three carbons and 8 hydrogens: $\ce{C3H8}$. Check it against the general formula: 2 × 3 + 2 = 8.

prompt: Use the general formula C_nH_{2n+2} the same way for butane, which has four carbons. How many hydrogen atoms does it have?
explain: 2 × 4 + 2 = 10, so butane is C₄H₁₀. Double the carbons, then add two.

text: 5. Using the general formula on a big molecule

md: The general formula earns its keep on molecules nobody draws. An alkane with 12 carbons has 2 × 12 + 2 = 26 hydrogens, so it is $\ce{C12H26}$. **Work the arithmetic out and write the finished formula** — examiners report answers left as "C₁₂H₂₄₊₂", which is a rule rather than a formula and earns nothing.

title: GCSE Chemistry - Hydrocarbons - Alkanes & Homologous Series
why: A second run through the family, the general formula and the names.

prompt: An alkane has 7 carbon atoms. Use CnH2n+2 to work out how many hydrogen atoms it has.
explain: 2 × 7 + 2 = 16. The rule works for any chain length, which is the whole point of having it.

title: Where this mark goes
md: Summer 2025's C2 Foundation report records the twelve-carbon alkane being left as an **unfinished formula** rather than worked out, and the name of the $\ce{C_nH_{2n}}$ family being given as *alkane* or *ethene* instead of **alkenes**.

prompt: Which general formula belongs to the alkanes?
explain: CnH2n+2 for the alkanes. CnH2n is the alkenes, and CnH2n+1OH the alcohols — worth keeping apart, because the paper asks you to name a family from its formula.

md:
give the four features of a **homologous series**, including *differ by CH₂*.
define a **hydrocarbon** with the word **only** in it.
recall the alkane general formula $\ce{C_nH_{2n+2}}$ and use it on any chain length.
name, write the molecular formula of, and draw the displayed formula of methane, ethane, propane and butane.
say that all four are **gases** at room temperature, and why the boiling points rise along the family.

Organic chemistry is Question 4 of the C2 paper, and examiners call it the hardest topic on the course. The first mark is usually a definition or a general formula; the last is a drawn structure. Stuck on a structure? Draw the carbon chain first and add hydrogens until every carbon shows four bonds. The Sheet below lists the traps.
